newsitem.title: UK: Ofgas director attacks government utility review.
newsitem.headline: Ofgas director attacks government utility review.

text.p: Ofgas Director General Clare Spottiswoode has criticised government plans to overhaul utility regulation, arguing that key consumer and environmental measures were unworkable.
"Utilities are no longer the monolithic organisations they used to be," she was quoted by the London Times saying.
"Competition in the gas market has been more revolutionary than was envisaged. What the government is proposing could have been done 10 years ago. It can't be done now," she said.

She did not believe it was possible to support measures like helping poor people pay for their fuel or promising energy savings by exerting pressure on companies like the pipeline group Transco which are not directly connected with consumers.
